children: is stepping up its efforts to attract content creators and put pressure on Netflix
, offering new incentives for digital producers and launching a feature designed to help creators reach more targeted audiences.
At the Made on YouTube conference this week, YouTube
is expected to announce new features for creators and viewers to improve content, better screen content to personal tastes, and a new tool for microdramas, according to The Wall Street Journal.

is also seen launching an AI storytelling assistant that can analyze scripts and rough cuts based on what has worked and what hasn’t. Live streamers will also be able to enable live AI dubbing from English to Spanish.
The innovations are aimed at keeping content creators from accepting generous financial packages to jump ship to Netflix
has seen popular kids' shows CrunchLabs, DannyGo!, and Ms. Rachel all migrate to Netflix with sharing agreements between the two. And although YouTube
gives creators 55% of the advertising revenue generated by their videos, Netflix
reportedly offers creators an “upfront plus costs” buyout that includes a fixed upfront fee and covers the cost of production plus a profit margin on top.

title: YouTube offering creators new tools, incentives to ward off Netflix
